digest.component_or_area: adapters/jira_family sub-seam and jira datacenter backend
propositions: Rebar cannot reconcile against self-hosted Jira Data Center because the existing adapter is Cloud-only, differing on REST API version (v2 vs v3), authentication (PAT bearer vs ACLI subprocess), and user identity (name vs accountId).

PR #120's separate adapter package forks shared logic (field maps, sanitizers, probe classifier) across two code paths without a contract boundary, creating maintenance debt and drift between Cloud and DC implementations.

Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) are loaded by file path via the dynamic loader, so relocating them requires loader changes; instead, shared logic must be extracted to jira_family/ with location-pinned modules dependency-inverted to import from it.

Value maps (status and priority) are already duplicated across three locations with divergence on the 'deleted' key; consolidating them in jira_family/ as a single source-of-truth requires deciding which definition (outbound_fields and config.py agree on 'deleted: Done'; jira_fields omits it) becomes canonical.

DC requires TLS-enforced connections with certificate verification always on, rejecting non-https base_url unless explicitly overridden with allow_insecure=true; the PAT credential must be environment-only, never in config files, and least-privilege service accounts must be operator-documented.

The epic acceptance criterion 'operator-attested bidirectional reconciliation with real data moving' was initially proven only for inbound (DC issue appears locally) and not for outbound (local edit appears in DC); live harness validation against an ephemeral Dockerized Jira 8.17.1 instance is required for both halves.
